newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to order checks of Boeing fuel-pump wiring.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to order checks of Boeing fuel-pump wiring.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Adminstration said on Friday it would issue an order next week to inspect wing fuel-pump wiring on some early Boeing 747s.

But it said that while the potential wiring problem was uncovered during the investigation of the crash of the Trans World Airlines 747 in the Atlantic off New York on July 17, it knew of no evidence to link the wiring to the crash.

Officials have not yet determined the cause of the explosion and crash of Flight 800 that killed all 230 people aboard. Some investigators think the 747's centre fuel tank may have exploded, but so far have no evidence to back this.
Thomas McSweeny, FAA director of aircraft certification, said the wiring is bundled with Teflon tape inside a metal conduit that runs through the wing fuel pumps and fuel tanks.
He said the wiring was near the engines and its insulation could be worn through by abrasion from engine vibration.

The inspections, to be completed in 90 days, can be done by pulling the wires out of the conduit, inspecting their Teflon coating and then returnng them to the conduit, McSweeny said. He added that the process was an overnight job.

He said the wiring was looked at in 1981, when some signs were found of abrasions. It was then coated with Teflon and encased in a stainless steel conduit to prevent a possible electric arc from burning through the conduit.
Asked about a link to Flight 800, McSweeny said, "There is no evidence from the accident site that we know of that links this wiring in this part of the wing to the cause of the accident."
